programElements.mission: The Defense Technical Information Center (DTIC) serves as the foundation of the Department of War's research and innovation ecosystem. As the central repository for all research and development activity—from planning through execution—DTIC is undergoing a pivotal transformation. By expanding its vast collections and integrating with advanced artificial intelligence and machine learning models, DTIC is evolving into a proactive tool for strategic foresight. This in turn will empower the Department with collective awareness, horizon scanning, and trend analysis, enabling DoW researchers to avoid duplication, deploy resources more efficiently and effectively, and deliver enhanced capabilities to our warfighters faster. The transformation of DTIC’s infrastructure and platform in support of an AI-enabled repository is a critical investment, designed to accelerate our technical maturity and secure decision advantage for senior leaders. To realize the full potential of its transformation, DTIC must cultivate strong partnerships across the research ecosystem. The vision of leveraging DoW’s strategic research assets and artificial intelligence and machine learning capabilities explicitly acknowledges that DTIC cannot achieve its goals in isolation. Strategic collaboration with the Joint Staff, military departments, Combatant Commands, Office of the Chief Digital and Artificial Intelligence Officer, OUSW Comptroller, DCAPE, DoW CIO, FFRDCs, etc. is paramount. These partnerships provide access to data sources, cutting-edge technologies, and specialized expertise, that are essential for a complete collection and rapid integration of AI/ML for sophisticated analysis.

projects.title: Information Analysis Centers
projects.mission: The Information Analysis Centers (IAC) program provides the essential, centralized capability that rapidly bridges the gap between DoW's sprawling scientific and technical research enterprise and the urgent need to field state of the art technological capabilities for the warfighter. The core challenge facing the DoW R&D community is the inability to efficiently locate, synthesize, and reuse technical data across disparate labs and organizations. This decentralized environment creates significant technical and financial risk, leading to unintentional duplication of effort, slower development cycles, and critical technological gaps. The IAC program directly mitigates these risks by serving as the primary nexus for technical collaboration. With an existing network of approximately 700 partner organizations, the IAC is a critical force multiplier that accelerates technology transition and development by performing three core functions: • Synthesizing Knowledge: Leveraging DTIC's repository to generate technical information analysis and products, enabling reuse and reducing technical risk for new programs. • Supporting Applied Research: Utilizing scientific and technical information (STI) to directly support ongoing basic and applied research, ensuring that "lessons learned" are integrated early in the development lifecycle. • Facilitating Complex Research: Executing primary research directly or jointly to solve interagency challenges where seamless STI sharing is a prerequisite. By centralizing and streamlining access to innovation, IAC provides a decisive strategic advantage, enabling program managers and developers to build upon a foundation of existing knowledge rather than starting from scratch.

programElements.peName: Management HQ - Defense Technical Information Center (DTIC)
programElements.mission: This program element (PE) provides funding for the Management Headquarters (HQ) element of the Defense Technical Information Center (DTIC), a DoW Field Activity. The PE supports personnel compensation for HQ-assigned civilians, along with related administrative and contract support costs. This PE was established in FY 2017, designed to support activities deemed as headquarters functions, with no operational efficiencies or enhancement to mission. This PE supports the following HQ functions and mission essential activities critical to the success of DTIC’s operations, and mandated by law or regulation: - Activity leadership, strategic planning, and Front Office support staff. -- The front office staff represents a small component of this PE. Most of the specialized functions and skill sets described below are centralized activities within the PE yet support the larger organization and its employees. These activities were consolidated to improve efficiencies throughout DTIC and are essential to the operation of DTIC’s primary PE 0605801KA. - Financial Management and Comptroller. Provides integrated resource management at the Agency level to obtain, control, and execute budget and manpower authorities to support the organization's mission requirements. Develops and prepares agency budget documents and exhibits for submission to both OSW and Congress. -- Accounting support to DTIC’s mission operations; partners with the Defense Finance and Accounting Service (DFAS) and Washington Headquarters Service (WHS) to present accurate financial reporting and Fund Balance with Treasury. -- Financial Improvement and Audit Remediation (FIAR) activities and oversight in compliance with the Department’s audit goals, objectives, and milestones. - Human Resources (HR) Liaison Support. Partners with DFAS to provide the DTIC enterprise with payroll processing and “Hire to Retire” mission support; oversees and organizes employee training, professional development, and staff certification programs (e.g., Acquisition, Financial Management, and IT programs). -- Coordinates recruitment placement and classification action for the mission areas; liaison to DFAS for HR servicing and the Defense Logistics Agency (DLA) for Equal Employment Opportunity (EEO) program maintenance. - Mandatory Records Management compliance activities and administration programs. - IT Management and DTIC Platform Management. Collects, analyzes, and reports information necessary to effectively and efficiently manage enterprise IT resources; functions are performed in compliance with DoW-CIO guidance, instructions and mandates and performed by a service provider through a SLA with the Defense Information Services Agency (DISA)in the case of DTIC internal needs and by infrastructure and platform services’ providers (currently the Department of the Air Force’s Cloud One; in transition to CDAO’s War Data Platform.
